newsitem.title: POLAND: Poles irate over denied church funeral.
newsitem.headline: Poles irate over denied church funeral.

text.p: Polish priests tried to explain to angry churchgoers on Sunday why a prominent pro-abortion gynaecologist had been denied a Roman Catholic burial last week in the city of Lodz.
"People, come to your senses," exhorted the preacher at St Andrew's Church in Warsaw.

"Professor (Waclaw) Dec was a declared non-believer who never darkened a church doorway, and he publicly advocated the killing of unborn infants. Allowing a Catholic funeral would have meant scandalising people."

Under Catholic canon Law, a funeral mass may be denied to heretics, apostates, schismatics, those who order cremation as a sign of religious defiance and others who have not retracted public violations of Church teachings.

Episcopate spokesman Bishop Tadeusz Pieronek issued a statement defending the church's refusal to give Dec a Catholic burial but the Polish media have largely publicised views critical of the decision.
"I am a practising Catholic but from today on I won't throw a penny into the collection basket," an irate woman told the daily Super Express in front of the locked church.

"Ten years ago the professor (Dec) saved my life and thanks to him I now have a seven-year-old son," another woman said. "To my mind he was a better Christian than the bishop," a middle-aged man told public television.
He was one of some 1,000 people who had come to pay their respects after seeing Dec's obituary in the press.
The requiem mass was denied on orders from the Archbishop of Lodz, Wladyslaw Ziolek.
At the last moment, Dec's family arranged for a graveside service conducted by a military chaplain not under the archbishop's jurisdiction.
Dec, who had headed the local Institute of Gynaecology and Obstetrics, had been a champion of abortion rights and several years ago had been voted Lodz's "Man of the Year".
